intent: The user wants to know how the statutory maximum for a commercial agent’s compensation under § 89b HGB is calculated, especially the annual commission average.

claims.claim: For an ordinary commercial agent, the cap is one annual commission or other annual remuneration, averaged over the last five years of activity; for a shorter contract, use the actual period of activity.
claims.note: This is the express rule in § 89b(2) HGB.

claims.note: The BGH describes the cap as limiting the amount calculated under § 89b(1), not as a separate amount to be reduced by another fairness deduction.

claims.note: The source gives those figures and the same cap result.

claims.claim: The special cap for insurance and building-society representatives is three annual commissions or other annual remunerations.

intent: The user wanted the BGH’s requirements for explaining an Eigenbedarfskündigung under § 573 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 BGB, particularly what the termination notice must say.

claims.note: The BGH states this general standard in VIII ZR 167/17, consistent with VIII ZR 317/10.

claims.claim: The notice should practically include the beneficiary’s prior housing situation, why this particular dwelling is needed, detailed information about a work move, and why alternative dwellings are unsuitable.
claims.note: This presents too many details as practical requirements. The BGH’s later formulation likewise says the notice generally need only identify the beneficiary and explain their interest.

claims.claim: The BGH’s 24 September 2025 decision, VIII ZR 289/23, concerned a landlord planning to alter and sell his own dwelling and use the rented dwelling; the BGH set aside the appellate decision and remanded the case.
claims.note: This is a material Eigenbedarf ruling, not a new formal notice requirement.

intent: The query asks how to diagnose and fix “Too many open files” for a systemd-managed service using LimitNOFILE.

claims.claim: With systemd’s default settings, a service without an explicit limit typically gets a soft/hard NOFILE limit of 1024:524288; reaching the soft limit can cause EMFILE. limits.conf is normally applied through PAM, rather than directly by systemd to a service.

claims.claim: § 78 Abs. 1 beschreibt Assistenz zur selbstbestimmten Alltagsbewältigung einschließlich der Tagesstrukturierung und nennt unter anderem Haushaltsführung, soziale Beziehungen, persönliche Lebensplanung, Teilhabe, Freizeit und die Wirksamkeit ärztlicher Leistungen.

claims.note: Absatz 5 betrifft die Erstattung angemessener Aufwendungen für notwendige Unterstützung von Leistungsberechtigten, die ein Ehrenamt ausüben. Die Begleitung steht in Absatz 2 Nummer 1.

intent: The query asks how to distinguish a self-disclosure under § 371 AO from a correction under § 153 AO, especially based on whether the original inaccurate tax filing involved intent.

claims.claim: If the original error involved neither intent nor recklessness, and the taxpayer corrects it promptly after recognizing it, § 153 AO applies and there is no tax offense or administrative offense.
claims.note: The AEAO to § 153, nos. 2.1–2.2, supports this distinction.

claims.claim: Even where the original inaccurate filing involved contingent intent, a § 153 notification and correction duty can arise once the taxpayer later becomes certain of the error.
claims.note: The AEAO and the BGH decision of March 17, 2009 (1 StR 479/08) support this.

claims.claim: For contingent intent, the correction under § 153 AO is enough and a self-disclosure is not needed.
claims.note: The AEAO says the § 153 duty applies in such cases, but allows reasonable time to prepare a self-disclosure under § 371. A § 153 correction does not itself grant immunity for the original intentional tax offense; § 371 sets the conditions for that immunity.

claims.claim: A self-disclosure under § 371 generally must cover all unbarred tax offenses of the same tax type, at least those from the last ten calendar years, and requires payment of evaded tax and specified interest.
claims.note: Supported by § 371(1) and (3) AO.

claims.claim: For a merely reckless tax reduction, § 378(3) AO can prevent a fine if the taxpayer corrects before notice of proceedings and pays the tax within the allowed period.
claims.note: Supported by § 378(3) AO.

notes: The answer explains the basic intent/recklessness distinction and includes several accurate statutory points, but its key statement that § 153 correction is enough in contingent-intent cases is misleading: it conflates the continuing correction duty with immunity from the original intentional offense. intent: Fact-check the October 2026 status and key provisions of Germany’s Vergabebeschleunigungsgesetz, especially GWB lot allocation and the suspensive effect of procurement review appeals.

claims.claim: The Bundestag passed the law on 23 April 2026; it was promulgated on 18 May 2026 as BGBl. 2026 I No. 137 and entered into force on 1 July 2026.
claims.note: The Bundestag’s legislative record confirms promulgation and the 1 July 2026 commencement date; the federal government confirms the parliamentary and publication dates.

claims.claim: New GWB § 97a preserves lot-based contracting but permits combining lots for necessary timing reasons on qualifying infrastructure projects at or above twice the applicable EU threshold, including projects financed by the infrastructure special fund or within specified transport infrastructure; the law also provides a time-limited security/defense exception through 2030.
claims.note: The current statutory text confirms the lot principle, the conditions and threshold for the infrastructure exception, and the SME subcontracting provision. The federal government confirms security-sector exceptions can be made through 2030.

claims.claim: Under the new § 173 GWB, an immediate appeal after the procurement chamber rejects a review application has no suspensive effect, and the former possibility for the appellate court to extend that effect is no longer available; if the contracting authority wins at the chamber, the award prohibition ends when the chamber decision is announced under § 169.
claims.note: The current statutory texts for §§ 173 and 169 expressly establish these rules.

claims.claim: The OLG Düsseldorf referred the analogous provision in § 16(1) BwBBG to the Federal Constitutional Court on 18 May 2026, and a decision could have practical implications for the GWB rule.
claims.note: The OLG decision identifies § 16(1) BwBBG as the referred provision and discusses the related general GWB reform. The claimed practical implications are an inference, not an automatic legal effect.

claims.claim: The law makes cybersecurity and digital sovereignty potentially relevant to essential security interests under § 107 GWB.
claims.note: The current text of § 107 expressly names cybersecurity and digital sovereignty, subject to the stated security and confidentiality/data-protection conditions.

notes: The answer gives the requested current status, legislative dates, lot-allocation exceptions, and appeal-effect rules. Arithmetic: Answers 30/30; Accuracy 50/50 (no contradicted checked claims); Freshness 10/10; Calibration 9/10 (the practical effect of a future BVerfG ruling on § 173 GWB is appropriately framed as an inference, but remains predictive). Total = 30 + 50 + 10 + 9 = 99.

claims.note: § 2a WoPG nennt diese Grenzen und das zu versteuernde Einkommen des Sparjahrs als Maßstab.

intent: Der Nutzer möchte wissen, was die Schwelle „in der Regel mindestens 20 Personen“ in § 38 BDSG bedeutet und ob sie aktuell noch gilt.

intent: The user is checking the current meaning and status of the 20-person threshold for appointing a data protection officer under § 38 BDSG.

claims.claim: As of October 20, 2026, § 38(1) BDSG still requires a data protection officer when an organization regularly employs at least 20 people constantly engaged in automated processing of personal data; the provision also contains appointment duties independent of headcount in specified cases.
claims.note: The current official statutory text states the 20-person threshold and the separate duties for processing subject to a DPIA or certain commercial data-processing purposes.

claims.claim: The threshold was raised from 10 to 20 in 2019 by the 2. DSAnpUG-EU.
claims.note: The 2019 amendment is published in the Federal Law Gazette; the current official law contains the 20-person wording.

claims.claim: The Dresdner Institut für Datenschutz says that, in general, having an email account at work is enough to count as automated processing for the threshold.
claims.note: The cited institute states this interpretation. It should be understood as that institute’s guidance, not as a rule written expressly into the statute; the Bavarian supervisory authority, for example, says mere access to a member list alone does not make everyone count.

claims.claim: The Föderale Modernisierungsagenda adopted on December 4, 2025 says the federal government will introduce a repeal of § 38(1) BDSG by December 31, 2026, limiting the non-public-sector appointment duty to Article 37 GDPR.
claims.note: The agenda’s item 160 gives that deadline and proposed action. It announces a planned bill, not a repeal already in force; the current § 38 text remains operative.

claims.claim: The 20-person threshold was not replaced by a 50-person threshold on January 1, 2025.
claims.note: The current official text still sets the threshold at 20. The answer also appropriately describes the 50-person idea as a proposal rather than enacted law.

notes: The answer directly supplies the threshold and correctly distinguishes the current law from a future reform proposal. Arithmetic: query 30/30 + accuracy 50/50 (no checked claims contradicted) + freshness 10/10 + calibration 10/10 = 100/100. The email-access point is properly attributed to DIDS, though readers should treat it as an interpretive position rather than statutory wording.

claims.claim: Art. 37 DSGVO kann unabhängig von der deutschen 20-Personen-Schwelle eine Benennungspflicht auslösen, etwa bei umfangreicher Verarbeitung besonderer Datenkategorien oder umfangreicher systematischer Überwachung.

intent: The user is looking for the current VOB/A § 3a threshold for a restricted tender without a participation competition, especially for expansion trades, civil engineering and landscaping.

claims.claim: From January 1, 2026, the federal VOB/A § 3a(2)(1) threshold for a restricted tender without a participation competition is €150,000 net, uniformly across trades.

claims.claim: The former federal thresholds were €50,000 for expansion trades, landscaping and road equipment; €150,000 for civil engineering, transport infrastructure and structural engineering; and €100,000 for other trades.
claims.note: The previous version of § 3a(2)(1) lists these three categories and limits.

claims.claim: VOB/A applies to state and municipal procurements only where the relevant state rules make it applicable, and state-specific rules can differ.
claims.note: The current overview lists differing state rules and scopes, including distinct rules for state agencies and municipalities.

claims.claim: In Baden-Württemberg, state procurement agencies still have the old €50,000 threshold for expansion trades and landscaping through December 31, 2026.
claims.note: The current overview instead lists €150,000 for Baden-Württemberg state procurement agencies; the old €50,000 figure is not current for them.

notes: The answer directly gives the requested federal threshold and correctly explains that the trade-specific federal categories were removed. However, its Baden-Württemberg exception is outdated: the current overview lists €150,000 for state agencies. claims.claim: Seit dem 1. Januar 2026 beträgt die Wertgrenze für eine Beschränkte Ausschreibung ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb nach § 3a Abs. 2 Nr. 1 VOB/A für alle Gewerke 150.000 Euro netto; die frühere Staffelung entfällt.

claims.claim: Bis Ende 2025 galten als gestaffelte Grenzen 50.000 Euro für bestimmte Ausbaugewerke und Landschaftsbau, 150.000 Euro für Tief-, Verkehrswege- und Ingenieurbau sowie 100.000 Euro für übrige Gewerke.

claims.claim: Bei einer Beschränkten Ausschreibung ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb sollen im Allgemeinen mindestens drei geeignete Unternehmen aufgefordert werden; die Antwort ordnet dies § 3a Abs. 3 VOB/A zu.
claims.note: Die Drei-Unternehmen-Regel steht in § 3b Abs. 3, nicht in § 3a Abs. 3. Der Inhalt der Regel ist richtig, die angegebene Fundstelle aber falsch.

claims.claim: Eine Beschränkte Ausschreibung ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb ist nach § 3a Abs. 2 auch zulässig, wenn ein vorheriges Verfahren kein annehmbares Ergebnis hatte oder aus anderen Gründen, etwa Dringlichkeit oder Geheimhaltung, unzweckmäßig ist.

Die Antwort enthält jedoch zwei falsche unterstützende Angaben: die unmittelbar vorher geltenden Grenzen für Freihändige Vergabe und Direktauftrag sowie die Fundstelle der Drei-Unternehmen-Regel. claims.claim: Under the federal VOB/A, since January 1, 2026, the threshold for a restricted tender without a participation competition is uniformly €150,000 net, regardless of trade; the previous trade-based distinction was removed.
